title: Bidirectional BFS in Tbilisi: Meet in the Middle
description: Watch Bidirectional BFS race across a map of Tbilisi, expanding from both start and goal points at once. The moment the two frontiers collide, the shortest route emerges—fast, clean, and graph-theory elegant.
ig_caption:
🚦✨ Bidirectional BFS is the “meet-in-the-middle” shortest path trick! 

In this visualization of street-like graphs inspired by Tbilisi’s Vake District, the algorithm treats intersections as nodes and roads as edges, then runs two BFS searches simultaneously: one from the start node and one from the goal node. Because BFS explores by increasing distance (unweighted edges), the first intersection where the frontiers meet lets us reconstruct an optimal path without exploring the entire map 🌍⚡

📌 Why it’s powerful (technical vibe):
- BFS guarantees shortest paths in unweighted graphs 🧠
- Bidirectional BFS reduces the explored search space from ~b^d to roughly ~b^(d/2) (where b is branching factor, d is path length) 📉
- We maintain visited sets/frontiers for both directions and stop as soon as an overlap appears 🔁

Try this on your own “real map” graph and see how quickly it converges! 👇 Share your favorite city map dataset or challenge routes in the comments—and follow for more algorithm street-walkthroughs 🗺️💻
